title: sales-partnership-scratch-notes-liam-chen
body:
Helix Financial — Account research + outbound + objection handling (scratchpad)

Last updated: 2025-02-20 by Liam Chen (copied Maya + Jordan)
Status: early outreach — target pilot conversation

Quick summary:
- Target: Helix Financial (mid-market fintech, ~1.2k employees, HQ NYC).
- Why them: heavy investment in real-time customer support, latency-sensitive fraud detection models, looking to reduce inference costs while maintaining sub-200ms tail latency for chat/agents. Public blog on migrating models in 2024 — suggests infra refresh.
- Primary ask we want: pilot Redwood Dedicated for customer support LLM + fallback to hosted for burst. Also sell observability + rollback policies.

Key contacts (to confirm via LinkedIn + Zoominfo):
- Priya Anand — Head of AI Platforms (decision influence, owns infra budget) — likely primary sponsor.
- Carlos Mendes — Director, Customer Ops (buyer for support workload) — cares about latency/availability and cost per ticket.
- Elena Rossi — SecOps (security/compliance gatekeeper) — needs private deploy + KMS.
- Joe Park — Lead ML Engineer (technical champion) — cares about batching, KV cache, quantization options and integration.

Observed signals/why now:
- Job postings for MLOps infra engineers (3 postings last quarter).
- Blog post: "Scaling model inference at Helix" (Oct 2024) — callout about cost of embeddings + experiments with quantized runtimes.
- Recent outage in support chat (public blip) — they'll prioritize reliability and graceful degradation.

Pain points (inferred):
- Unit cost of serving embeddings and chat is high (~$0.12/1000 tokens per their disclosed numbers)
- Tail latency spikes during peak support hours — current fallback is slow (stateless endpoints)
- Security/compliance constraints for PII — need KMS + audit logs for any external provider
- Lack of visibility across models and routes — ops team relies on ad-hoc dashboards

Value props to emphasize (short):
- Predictable, reserved capacity (Dedicated) to hit latency SLOs and reduce tail spikes
- Cost controls: batching, caching, and quantization recommendations tailored to their workloads
- Private deployment option with KMS/HSM and audit logging for compliance
- Rollouts & fallbacks: canary/A-B and automatic fallback to cheaper model variants during pressure
- Observability: token-level cost + latency breakdowns, route dashboards (helps Carlos + Priya)

Outbound cold email draft (short A/B test):
Subject A: "Cut inference costs for Helix support by 25% (pilot)"
Subject B: "Reduce chat latency spikes — Redwood pilot idea"
Body (short):
Hi Priya — quick note,
I saw Helix’s post on scaling inference and noticed latency/cost tradeoffs that sound familiar. We recently helped a fintech reduce tail latency spikes and cut per-ticket inference cost by ~30% using a mix of reserved capacity + KV caching.
Would you be open to a 20–30 min pilot planning call next week to see if a small Dedicated pilot for support chat makes sense? I can share a quick cost/latency model tailored to Helix.
Thanks,
Liam

Longer outreach (if reply shows technical interest):
- Attach mini-runbook: integration touchpoints (1) API keys + VPC setup (2) model pinning & rollout plan (3) perf validation tests

Call script (first intro with Priya / Joe):
1) Quick intros (2m)
2) Context: why I'm reaching out — saw the Helix blog + job postings (1m)
3) Confirm problems: cost, tail latency, compliance (ask specific metrics) (5m)
   - "What's your current p50/p95 latency for support chat? Any hard SLOs?"
   - "How are you handling embeddings at scale? Any compression/quantization experiments?"
4) High-level how Redwood helps (4m) — Dedicated, caching, batching, private option, KMS
5) Pilot ask (3m): propose a 6-week pilot:
   - Week 0–1: integration + smoke tests (private control plane + networking)
   - Week 2–4: run traffic on dedicated pool, collect metrics (latency, cost, error rate)
   - Week 5–6: tuning, rollout plan for production + rollback policy
6) Next steps & commit to deliverables (1m)

Objection handling (common) — shorthand responses:
- "We can’t expose PII / we need on-prem": Redwood Private + on-prem packaging available; propose air-gapped eval or private VPC with KMS. Ask: any legal review template we should fill?
- "We’re happy with current cloud provider endpoints": Acknowledge, then pitch hybrid: start with non-sensitive traffic or embeddings, compare tail latency + cost with a short A/B run. Emphasize minimal integration (same REST/SDK).
- "We don’t have cycles for integration": Offer turnkey pilot (we provide runbook + engineering time via solutions-eng) and can do a 2-week POC with limited dev time.
- "Cost savings sound theoretical": Promise a baseline audit (free) — share model of current spend vs projected with batching/caching. Offer to run 48-hour bench with their sample traffic to prove delta.

Technical FAQ to prep for Joe (quick bullets):
- Integration: REST/SDK, streaming responses, tool-calling supported.
- Latency: Dedicated gives predictable p95; can pin models and use kernel selection for perf.
- Caching: prefix/KV cache to cut repeated prefix cost (good for support conversations)
- Quantization: recommend per-workload quantization profile (we can run evals)
- Observability: token-level cost and per-route dashboards + tracing hooks

Metrics I want to collect before first call (ask them to share if possible):
- Current throughput (requests/min) for support chat and embeddings jobs
- p50/p95/p99 latency per endpoint
- Current monthly spend on inference (or per-1000-token cost they observe)
- Any SLOs and error budgets

Attachments to prep (action items):
- Quick Helix-tailored cost model (spreadsheet) — Liam (due: 2025-02-22)
- Short runbook for pilot + integration checklist — Solutions Eng template + customize (ask Jordan to prep)
- Example case study (fintech) — Maya to pull and redact numbers (due: 2025-02-21)

Open questions / things to confirm on call:
- Who signs off on pilot budget? (Procurement vs Infra vs Product)
- Any required legal/contractual templates for Private deployment? (NDA / DPA specifics)
- Are there existing contracts for model vendors we need to consider?

To-do (near-term):
- [ ] Finalize cost model spreadsheet (Liam) — 2025-02-22
- [ ] Pull fintech case study + redacted metrics (Maya) — 2025-02-21
- [ ] Draft pilot runbook + engineering touchpoints (Jordan) — 2025-02-24
- [ ] Quick LinkedIn/Zoominfo verification of contacts (Liam) — 2025-02-18 (inflight)
- [ ] A/B subject line test set in outreach tool (Liam + SDR) — 2025-02-20

Notes to self (unpolished):
- Try to get Priya on a short call first (sponsor) then bring Joe for tech deep-dive.
- Emphasize our hybrid deployment story to overcome security objections.
- If they push back on price, lead with cost model + ability to granularly cap spend + reserved capacity pricing.
- Keep first email short — one clear ask (20–30m call).

Raw snippets / quick drafts:
- "We helped a fintech cut inference tails by 40% using reserved GPU pools + KV cache; pilot takes ~6 weeks."
- Quick pitch line for Carlos: "Reduce per-ticket inference cost and make slow hours less painful — measurable impact on support KPIs."

End of scratchpad.

-- Liam
